data.analysis: Choose N=3: the supplied source and measurements reveal three useful, complementary avenues—using the currently ignored thread budget, executing independent options in SIMD lanes, and reducing scalar work while retaining the supplied formula and CND coefficients. More trees would split overlapping math work without evidence of another independent bottleneck. The baseline is valid, with three samples of 7.5237, 7.5372, and 7.5250 ms (mean 7.5286 ms; score 0.5). The entrypoint currently calls the serial kernel and does not use threads; the supplied environment sets OMP_NUM_THREADS=40, but that does not establish the threads argument for every call. SIMD code should rely only on ISA enabled by the frozen build, use safe loads because the five array starts need not all be 64-byte aligned, and retain a scalar fallback and tail. Preserve the full input-dependent computation and validate all varied inputs against the stated tolerance. Only src/candidate.cpp is in scope.

children.objective: Explore OpenMP parallelization of the outer per-option loop in src/candidate.cpp, with a serial path for small workloads or a one-thread budget and a static partition as a starting point. Respect the passed threads budget rather than relying on OMP_NUM_THREADS; ensure every output element is written exactly once and all inputs are processed. Measure multiple valid n/thread combinations under the unchanged protocol and retain only correctness-passing variants.
children.subject: OpenMP execution within the threads budget

children.objective: Explore a standalone SIMD kernel across independent options using only x86 ISA enabled by the frozen build, with compile-time guards and a correct scalar fallback/tail. Keep the supplied Black-Scholes expression and CND coefficients; assess vector math or other precision-sensitive changes against the fixed tolerance on varied per-element inputs. Do not change threading in this tree, so its SIMD contribution can be measured separately and tested in later combinations.
children.subject: SIMD across independent options

children.objective: Explore scalar-only instruction reduction in the existing calculation, such as sharing sqrtf(T) and evaluating the same CND polynomial in Horner form while preserving its coefficients and mathematical expression. Avoid changing the CND approximation or introducing an alternate answer path. Record whether the compiler already performs these transformations, validate rounding changes on varied inputs, and compare timings with the same protocol.
children.subject: Scalar arithmetic reduction with the supplied CND
